newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA HAS $20 MLN CAPITAL ACCOUNT GAP 1996.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA HAS $20 MLN CAPITAL ACCOUNT GAP 1996.

text.p: Bulgaria posted a capital account deficit of $20 million last year after a $113.8 million gap in 1995, Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) preliminary figures showed.

Portfolio investments' net change for the last year was $167 million as liabilities to foreign lenders decreased by $120.7 million, mainly due to maturity payments on Bulbank's Eurobonds, and the country's assets abroad rose by $46.3 million, the BNB said in a statement.
Bulgaria received $339.5 million principal payments on long-term loans to other countries last year.
Local commercial banks' deposits abroad fell by $68.2 million in 1996 after falling by $171.4 million the year before.
Capital outflow in 1996 totalled $1,007.3 million, including a resident capital outflow of $797.3 million due to low confidence in Bulgaria's shaky banking system.
Net principal payments on long-term and short-term loans from foreigh lenders totalled $298.9 million in 1996 against $306.4 million the year before.
BNB foreign exchange reserves fell by $751.2 million last year to $407.6 million, BNB figures showed. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
